## Why visit

The strongest city-centre starting point when breadth of beer and cider matters as much as old pub character. A substantial changing cask range sits alongside continental bottles and other draught styles, so experienced drinkers can compare local discoveries without treating every stop as a single-pint transaction. The 1930s building and nautical bar add character; the upstairs Art Deco room is a separate architectural attraction when accessible. It also supplies one of the most useful meal stops on a Dale Street route, making it practical to settle in rather than hurry through.

## Beer

CAMRA records eight changing cask beers; the pub also maintains a broad continental and bottled selection. CAMRA names Black Lodge and Colbier among changing suppliers, but does not identify a reliable permanent cask-beer line.

## Food

One Pan Band kitchen: official menu includes beef scouse, vegetarian blind scouse and other pub dishes; menus change.

## Plan the visit

Pub and CAMRA kitchen hours disagree, particularly early in the week. Confirm food service directly. Upstairs access may depend on events.

**Getting there:** Dale Street, near the Queensway tunnel entrance; Moorfields is the nearby rail option.
